name: Bus Clarity
description: On a bus of many parts, such as drums or keys: the parts that hide each other drawn apart, a little each way.

name: All the Way
description: Recover and Tame at their tops: as far as it goes, to hear what it does on a mix; usually too much to keep.

name: Bright and Clear
description: Both ways at their middle with the unmasking leaning to the highs: what is hidden in the top comes out first, for a dark mix.

name: Clear Master
description: Both ways past their middle: a mix whose parts sit on each other comes apart into its parts, at the loudness it came in at.

name: Gentle Balance
description: A light hand each way: what is hidden comes up a little and what hides it goes down a little, so a master opens without anyone hearing an equaliser. Where to start.

name: Late Night
description: Nothing unmasked, Boost down 8 dB: the leaner bass and forward middle of a mix played quietly.

name: Lift the Detail
description: Mostly bringing up, with more of the spectrum given to it: the quiet parts that the loud ones hide, a reverb's tail, a shaker under the drums, the breath of a voice, come forward, and little is taken from the rest.

name: Played Loud
description: Nothing unmasked, Boost up 8 dB: the fuller bass and lighter middle of a mix played louder, at the same loudness.

name: Tame Resonances
description: Tame with Bias down, so only what stands well out of the rest is turned down: ringing peaks and resonances, and little else.

name: Tame the Mud
description: Mostly turning down, kept between 80 and 600 Hz: a low middle that covers what is above it is held back where it does, and the rest is left alone.

name: Warm and Even
description: The unmasking leaning to the lows, with a little Boost: for a harsh, bright mix, the manual's own advice.

name: De-ess
description: Tame alone between 4.5 and 10 kHz, Bias down: an s that covers the rest of the voice is turned down where it does, and nothing outside the range is touched.
